Irrationality of the dilogarithm at 1/31/3

Ruiyi Zhang Independent Researcher, Columbia, Maryland, USA
Abstract.

We prove that Li2⁡(1/3)\operatorname{Li}_{2}(1/3) is irrational. Irrationality of Li2⁡(1/s)\operatorname{Li}_{2}(1/s) was known for integers s≤−5s\leq-5 and s≥6s\geq 6 by work of Hata and of Rhin and Viola, and Prellberg recently proved it for s=−4,5,−3s=-4,5,-3. We define polynomials Gm⁢(T)G_{m}(T) with rational coefficients by an interpolation determinant. The rank of this determinant modulo primes pp with m/8<p<5⁢m/4m/8<p<5m/4 bounds the denominators of the coefficients. A concavity inequality for a logarithmic energy, combined with the inversion v↦3/vv\mapsto 3/v, bounds Gm⁢(Li2⁡(1/3))G_{m}(\operatorname{Li}_{2}(1/3)). Interval arithmetic is used only for the energy and the potentials of a printed reference measure, on a uniform dyadic subdivision. The integral of the local rank function is a rational sum over 7676 printed affine pieces. The coefficients of G4G_{4} and the 9×99\times 9 determinant modulo 1717 are printed and can be checked by hand. A congruence modulo 1717 shows that Gm⁢(ξ)≠0G_{m}(\xi)\neq 0 for every rational ξ\xi and m=4⋅17tm=4\cdot 17^{t}, tt large in terms of ξ\xi.

Key words and phrases:
dilogarithm, irrationality, interpolation determinant, logarithmic energy, interval arithmetic
2020 Mathematics Subject Classification:
Primary 11J72; Secondary 33B30

1. Introduction

For |z|≤1|z|\leq 1 let Li2⁡(z)=∑k≥1zk/k2\operatorname{Li}_{2}(z)=\sum_{k\geq 1}z^{k}/k^{2}. Hata [5, Theorem 1.1] proved that Li2⁡(1/s)\operatorname{Li}_{2}(1/s) is irrational for every integer s≤−5s\leq-5 and every s≥7s\geq 7. Rhin and Viola settled s=6s=6 by their permutation group method [10, Section 6], and later treated negative arguments [11, Theorem 2.1 and Section 4]. Viola and Zudilin [13] introduced a six-parameter family of double integrals for dilogarithmic values. In 2024 Calegari, Dimitrov and Tang [2, Remark 2.8.2 and Section 15.2] listed the integers still open: s∈{−4,−3,−2,2,3,4,5}s\in\{-4,-3,-2,2,3,4,5\}. Prellberg’s 2026 preprint [9, Theorem 1.1] proves the cases s=−4,5,−3s=-4,5,-3. We prove the case s=3s=3. Our linear forms are values of an interpolation determinant of size 9⁢n9n, in place of the double integrals of [5, 9, 10, 13]. The rank of this determinant modulo primes controls the denominators of its coefficients.

Theorem 1.

The number Li2⁡(1/3)\operatorname{Li}_{2}(1/3) is irrational.

By Landen’s identity [8, (25.12.3)], Li2⁡(1/3)+Li2⁡(−1/2)=−12⁢log2⁡(3/2)\operatorname{Li}_{2}(1/3)+\operatorname{Li}_{2}(-1/2)=-\frac{1}{2}\log^{2}(3/2), and log⁡(3/2)\log(3/2) is transcendental by the Hermite–Lindemann theorem, a special case of [1, Theorem 1.4]. So Landen’s identity does not reduce the case s=3s=3 to the case s=−2s=-2.

Put θ=Li2⁡(1/3)\theta=\operatorname{Li}_{2}(1/3) and m=4⁢nm=4n. Section 2 defines Gm⁢(T)∈ℚ⁢[T]G_{m}(T)\in\mathbb{Q}[T] by an interpolation determinant. Sections 3 and 4 give

deg⁡Gm≤m⁢by Lemma 2.1,Km⁢Gm⁢(T)∈ℤ⁢[T],Km∈ℚ>0,\displaystyle\deg G_{m}\leq m\ \text{by Lemma~{}\ref{lem:moment-identity}},% \qquad K_{m}G_{m}(T)\in\mathbb{Z}[T],\qquad K_{m}\in\mathbb{Q}_{>0},
lim supm→∞4∣mlog⁡Kmm2≤τ<3.87273,\displaystyle\limsup_{\begin{subarray}{c}m\to\infty\\ 4\mid m\end{subarray}}\frac{\log K_{m}}{m^{2}}\leq\tau<3.87273,
(1.1) log⁡|Gm⁢(θ)|≤−3.8757⁢m2+C⁢m⁢log⁡m(m=4⁢n≥4).\displaystyle\log|G_{m}(\theta)|\leq-3.8757\,m^{2}+C\,m\log m\quad(m=4n\geq 4).

The exact value of τ\tau is in (3.12), and 3.87573.8757 is a lower bound for the constant of (4.5). The finite constant CC of Lemma 4.4 depends only on the reference measure. Since 3.87273<3.87573.87273<3.8757, the quadratic exponent is negative. If θ=u/q0\theta=u/q_{0} with q0>0q_{0}>0, then q0m⁢Km⁢Gm⁢(θ)∈ℤq_{0}^{m}K_{m}G_{m}(\theta)\in\mathbb{Z}. Section 5 shows that it is nonzero for m=4⋅17tm=4\cdot 17^{t} and tt large, and (1.1) shows that it tends to zero.

The only numerical margin in the proof is α0−τ>0\alpha_{0}-\tau>0. The size of CC is not used. Lemma 4.2 is computer-assisted. It is proved by interval arithmetic on the reference measure of Tables C.1 and C.2, over the uniform subdivision of Lemma C.1. The integral (3.8) is an exact sum over the 7676 affine pieces of Table A.2, each determined by the explicit lines of Table A. Tables 2.1, A and A.2 and (5.2) can be checked by hand. Python scripts recheck Lemma 4.2 and part of the remaining proof (Appendix D). Apart from this lemma, the proof is complete without them.

The proof uses three classical inputs.

Fact 1 (prime number theorem [4, Theorems 6 and 420, §§1.8 and 22.4]).

θCh⁢(y)=∑p≤ylog⁡p\theta_{\rm Ch}(y)=\sum_{p\leq y}\log p satisfies θCh⁢(y)/y→1\theta_{\rm Ch}(y)/y\to 1 as y→∞y\to\infty.

Only this qualitative form is used.

Fact 2 ([12, Lemma I.1.8]).

If σ\sigma is a real compactly supported signed measure of total mass zero with ∬|log⁡|u−w|⁢|d|⁢σ⁢|(u)⁢d|⁢σ|⁢(w)<∞\iint|\log|u-w||\,d|\sigma|(u)\,d|\sigma|(w)<\infty, then ∬log⁡|u−w|⁢d⁢σ⁢(u)⁢𝑑σ⁢(w)≤0\iint\log|u-w|\,d\sigma(u)\,d\sigma(w)\leq 0.

A short proof is given in Appendix E.

Fact 3 (Cauchy–Vandermonde [7, Theorem 25], [3, Section 2]).

For s=(s1,…,sm)s=(s_{1},\ldots,s_{m}), v=(v1,…,vL)v=(v_{1},\ldots,v_{L}) and h=L−m≥0h=L-m\geq 0,

det(((si′+vb)−1)1≤i′≤m, 1≤b≤L(vbℓ−1)1≤ℓ≤h, 1≤b≤L)=Δ⁢(s)⁢Δ⁢(v)∏i′,b(si′+vb),Δ⁢(u)=∏i<j(uj−ui).\det\begin{pmatrix}((s_{i^{\prime}}+v_{b})^{-1})_{1\leq i^{\prime}\leq m,\,1% \leq b\leq L}\\ (v_{b}^{\ell-1})_{1\leq\ell\leq h,\,1\leq b\leq L}\end{pmatrix}=\frac{\Delta(s% )\Delta(v)}{\prod_{i^{\prime},b}(s_{i^{\prime}}+v_{b})},\qquad\Delta(u)=\prod_% {i<j}(u_{j}-u_{i}).

A proof, including the sign, is given in the proof of Lemma 2.2.

Lemma C.1.

Let dx=9d_{x}=9, dv=8d_{v}=8, dz=7d_{z}=7, d∘=8d_{\circ}=8. Bisect every initial piece of the support ss to depth dsd_{s}: a piece [A,B][A,B] gives the 2ds2^{d_{s}} leaves

[A+(B−A)⁢(j−1)⁢2−ds,A+(B−A)⁢j⁢2−ds],1≤j≤2ds,[A+(B-A)(j-1)2^{-d_{s}},\,A+(B-A)j2^{-d_{s}}],\qquad 1\leq j\leq 2^{d_{s}},

in qq on the real supports and in tt on the circle. The leaves of each support have rational endpoints, disjoint interiors and union equal to the support. There are 132⋅29132\cdot 2^{9}, 145⋅28145\cdot 2^{8}, 106⋅27106\cdot 2^{7} and 32⋅2832\cdot 2^{8} leaves, 126464126464 in all (Table C.3).

Proof.

Within a piece the leaves are consecutive and their lengths add up to B−AB-A. The pieces of a support are consecutive and cover it. The counts are products. ∎

The leaves are the closed pieces of the proof of Lemma 4.2. On each of them the bound of that proof is below the cap, so no piece needs a finer subdivision.

Appendix D Computer checks

The ancillary scripts recheck printed data and run finite tests (Table D). They use exact rational arithmetic and, for the analytic bounds, Arb ball arithmetic [6] through python-flint 0.9.0 under Python 3.12.3.

Use of AI tools

The author devised the method of proof. Codex (OpenAI, GPT-6.1 Sol) computed the reference measure ν\nu and the other printed data, and wrote the Python scripts in anc/. Claude Code (Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5) checked the scripts, the data and the tables. The author checked every step of the proof, every table and every reference, and takes full responsibility for the content of the paper.
